preconditions.expression: T == int(stdin.split()[0]) and T >= 1 and T <= 10**3
preconditions.description: The first line of input is an integer T (1 ≤ T ≤ 10³) representing the number of test cases.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= N <= 10**6 for N in [int(line) for line in stdin.split() if line.isdigit() and int(line) <= 10**6])
preconditions.description: For each test case, the first line is an integer N (1 ≤ N ≤ 10⁶) representing the number of nodes in the tree.

preconditions.expression: all(len(edges) == N - 1 for N, edges in zip([int(line) for line in stdin.split() if line.isdigit()], [stdin.split()[i:i+N-1] for i in range(1, len(stdin.split()), N)]))
preconditions.description: Each test case has exactly N-1 edges, each represented as two integers u and v (1 ≤ u, v ≤ N) denoting an undirected edge between nodes u and v.

preconditions.expression: all(len(A) == N for N, A in zip([int(line) for line in stdin.split() if line.isdigit()], [list(map(int, line.split())) for line in stdin.split() if line.isdigit() and len(line.split()) == N]))
preconditions.description: Each test case has exactly N integers A₁, A₂, ..., Aₙ (0 ≤ Aᵢ ≤ 10⁹) representing the values of the nodes.

preconditions.expression: all(0 <= A_i <= 10**9 for A in [list(map(int, line.split())) for line in stdin.split() if line.isdigit() and len(line.split()) == N] for A_i in A)
preconditions.description: Each node value Aᵢ is a non-negative integer (0 ≤ Aᵢ ≤ 10⁹).

preconditions.expression: all(is_tree(N, edges) for N, edges in zip([int(line) for line in stdin.split() if line.isdigit()], [stdin.split()[i:i+N-1] for i in range(1, len(stdin.split()), N)]))
preconditions.description: The input graph is always a tree (connected and acyclic) rooted at node 1.

preconditions.expression: all(is_secure_tree(N, edges, A) for N, edges, A in zip([int(line) for line in stdin.split() if line.isdigit()], [stdin.split()[i:i+N-1] for i in range(1, len(stdin.split()), N)], [list(map(int, line.split())) for line in stdin.split() if line.isdigit() and len(line.split()) == N]))
preconditions.description: The input tree is initially secure, meaning for every leaf node u, the bitwise OR of all values on the path from root to u (Lᵤ) is greater than 0.

postconditions.expression: all(len(output_lines) == T for T, output_lines in zip([int(stdin.split()[0])], [stdout.split()]))
postconditions.description: The output contains exactly T lines, one for each test case.
Each output line is a non-negative integer representing the minimum possible security of the tree after zero or more operations.

postconditions.expression: all(min_security == compute_min_security(N, edges, A) for N, edges, A, min_security in zip([int(line) for line in stdin.split() if line.isdigit()], [stdin.split()[i:i+N-1] for i in range(1, len(stdin.split()), N)], [list(map(int, line.split())) for line in stdin.split() if line.isdigit() and len(line.split()) == N], [int(line) for line in stdout.split()]))
postconditions.description: For each test case, the output is the minimum possible security of the tree such that after every operation (setting Aᵤ = 0 for any node u), the tree remains secure (Lᵤ > 0 for every leaf node u). The security is the sum of Lᵤ for all leaf nodes u.

postconditions.expression: all(0 <= min_security <= sum(A) for min_security, A in zip([int(line) for line in stdout.split()], [list(map(int, line.split())) for line in stdin.split() if line.isdigit() and len(line.split()) == N]))
postconditions.description: The minimum security is a non-negative integer not exceeding the sum of all node values in the tree.
